newsitem.title: USA: U.S. poet James Dickey dies aged 73.
newsitem.headline: U.S. poet James Dickey dies aged 73.

text.p: Poet and novelist James Dickey died late on Sunday of complications from a bronchial infection, an official at the South Carolina hospital where he died said on Monday.
Pat Browder, nursing supervisor at Providence Hospital in Columbia, said Dickey, 73, who had been suffering from a lung disease, had been in the hospital since Wednesday.

Dickey was best known for his first novel, "Deliverance," which was made into a motion picture starring Burt Reynolds and John Voight, but he considered himself a poet first. He had lived in South Carolina's capital since the mid-1960s and taught for 25 years at the University of South Carolina.

Stories about the blustery, swaggering writer were legend, many of them wild and shocking. He used a blowgun to hunt rattlesnakes, made drunken trips through whitewater rapids and had a reputation for flirting at academic gatherings.
His work won national awards including the National Book Award in 1966. In 1987, he was inducted into the American Academy of Arts and letters.

Born in Atlanta on Feb. 2, 1923, Dickey attended what was then Clemson A&M College but dropped out to join the Army Air Corps. After the Second World War he earned bachelor's and master's degrees from Vanderbilt University.

He taught at Rice University and the University of Florida and served in the Air Force in the Korean War. He then went to work for advertising agencies in Atlanta and New York, handling such accounts as Coca-Cola and Delta, but he quit his job when his first book of poetry was published in 1960.
"He was the only genius I ever met," said Matthew Bruccoli, a professor of English at the University of South Carolina and a friend.

Survivors include Dickey's sons, Kevin and Christopher, from his first marriage to Maxine Syerson, who died in 1948, and his daughter Bronwen, from his second marriage to Deborah Dodson, from whom he separated.
Private funeral services will be held. The family also plans a memorial service in Columbia but details have not been announced.
